messages.author: 6c59377cefb23d12
messages.subject: Beginner help
parts:
Hi all,

I'm just starting to learn how to use ggplot2 and am extremely
impressed with both the software and the community that has developed
around it. My plots are looking better than ever and many of my
colleagues have taken note. Kudos to all involved!

My question is how to merge these two plots into a single one:

ggplot(data) + eas(x='signal') + geom_density()

ggplot(data) + eas(x='signal',color='factor(bin)') + geom_density()

I can get a beautiful density plot of my signal and another for the
density by "bin". What I'm having trouble with is combining both
plots into a single one.

Am I missing something obvious? Any help will be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,
-Kevin

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Beginner help
parts:
Kevin,

Something like this?

ggplot(data, aes(x= signal)) + geom_density() + geom_density(aes(colour
= bin))

HTH,

Thierry

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Beginner help
parts:
I not aware of a nice way to do that. But here is a quick hack. This will give you an extra 'bin' class with the marginal data.
 
tmp <- data
tmp$bin <- "Marginal"
data <- rbind(data, bin)
ggplot(data, aes(x = signal, colour = bin)) + geom_density()
 

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
